basedpyright.analysis.stubPath.description: Path to directory containing custom type stub files.

basedpyright.analysis.baselineFile.markdownDescription: Path to the baseline file. Defaults to `./.basedpyright/baseline.json`

basedpyright.analysis.inlayHints.variabl.description: Whether to show inlay hints on assignments to variables.

basedpyright.analysis.autoFormatStrings.markdownDescription: Whether to automatically insert an `f` in front of a string when typing a `{` inside it.

basedpyright.analysis.configFilePath.markdownDescription: Path to the directory or file containing the Pyright configuration (`pyrightconfig.json` or `pyproject.toml`). If a directory is specified, basedpyright will search for the config file in that directory. This is useful for monorepo structures where the config file is in a subdirectory. Example: `${workspaceFolder}/backend`

basedpyright.analysis.inlayHints.callArg.description: Whether to show inlay hints on function arguments.

enumDescriptions: Analyzes and reports errors on only open files.
Analyzes and reports errors on all files in the workspace.

basedpyright.analysis.inlayHints.callArg.description: Whether to show inlay hints on function arguments when the input expression is a variable with the same name as the parameter.

basedpyright.analysis.logLevel.description: Specifies the level of logging for the Output panel

basedpyright.analysis.inlayHints.functio.description: Whether to show inlay hints on function return types.

basedpyright.analysis.inlayHints.generic.description: Whether to show inlay hints on inferred generic types.

basedpyright.analysis.typeCheckingMode.description: Defines the default rule set for type checking.

basedpyright.analysis.useTypingExtension.markdownDescription: Whether to rely on imports from the `typing_extensions` module when targeting older versions of python that do not include certain typing features such as the `@override` decorator.

basedpyright.analysis.exclude.description: Paths of directories or files that should not be included. These override the include directories, allowing specific subdirectories to be excluded. Note that files in the exclude paths may still be included in the analysis if they are referenced (imported) by source files that are not excluded. Paths may contain wildcard characters ** (a directory or multiple levels of directories), * (a sequence of zero or more characters), or ? (a single character). If no exclude paths are specified, pyright automatically excludes the following: `**/node_modules`, `**/__pycache__`, `.git` and any virtual environment directories.

basedpyright.analysis.typeshedPaths.description: Paths to look for typeshed modules.

basedpyright.analysis.ignore.description: Paths of directories or files whose diagnostic output (errors and warnings) should be suppressed even if they are an included file or within the transitive closure of an included file. Paths may contain wildcard characters ** (a directory or multiple levels of directories), * (a sequence of zero or more characters), or ? (a single character). If no value is provided, the value of python.linting.ignorePatterns (if set) will be used.

basedpyright.analysis.useLibraryCodeForT.description: Use library implementations to extract type information when type stub is not present.

basedpyright.analysis.diagnosticSeverity.markdownDescription: Allows a user to override the severity levels for individual diagnostics. Use the rule name as a key and one of "error", "warning", "information", "none", `true` (alias for "error") or `false` (alias for "none") as value. The default value shown for each diagnostic is the default when "basedpyright.analysis.typeCheckingMode" is set to "standard". See [here](https://docs.basedpyright.com/latest/configuration/config-files/#diagnostic-settings-defaults) for defaults for each type checking mode ("off", "basic", "standard", "strict", and "all").

reportMatchNotExhaustive.description: Diagnostics for 'match' statements that do not exhaustively match all possible values.

reportUnreachable.description: Diagnostics for code that is determined by type analysis to be unreachable.

reportImplicitOverride.description: Diagnostics for overridden methods that do not include an `@override` decorator.

reportAny.description: Diagnostics for expressions with the `Any` type

reportExplicitAny.description: Diagnostics for type annotations that use the `Any` type

reportIgnoreCommentWithoutRule.description: Diagnostics for `# type: ignore` and `# pyright: ignore` comments without specifying a rule

reportPrivateLocalImportUsage.description: Diagnostics for incorrect usage of symbol imported from a non-"py.typed" module that is not re-exported from that module. Should be used along with `reportNonPrivateImportUsage`

reportImplicitRelativeImport.description: Diagnostics for non-relative imports that do not specify the full path to the module

reportUnsafeMultipleInheritance.description: Diagnostics for multiple inheritance where a base class's constructor may not get called

reportGeneralTypeIssues.description: Diagnostics for general type inconsistencies, unsupported operations, argument/parameter mismatches, etc. Covers all of the basic type-checking rules not covered by other rules. Does not include syntax errors.

reportImplicitAbstractClass.description: Diagnostics for abstract classes that do not explicitly extend `ABC`

reportPropertyTypeMismatch.description: Diagnostics for property whose setter and getter have mismatched types.

reportIncompatibleUnannotatedOverride.description: Diagnostics for overrides in subclasses that redefine a variable without a type annotation in an incompatible way

reportFunctionMemberAccess.description: Diagnostics for member accesses on functions.

reportUnannotatedClassAttribute.description: Diagnostics for class variable declarations that do not have a type annotation, which is required due to performance reasons for strict validation of subclasses

reportMissingImports.description: Diagnostics for imports that have no corresponding imported python file or type stub file.

reportInvalidAbstractMethod.description: Diagnostics for usages of `@abstractmethod` on a non-abstract class

reportMissingModuleSource.description: Diagnostics for imports that have no corresponding source file. This happens when a type stub is found, but the module source file was not found, indicating that the code may fail at runtime when using this execution environment. Type checking will be done using the type stub.

reportSelfClsDefault.description: Diagnostics for providing a default value for a `self` or `cls` parameter

reportInvalidTypeForm.description: Diagnostics for type expression that uses an invalid form.

reportMissingTypeStubs.description: Diagnostics for imports that have no corresponding type stub file (either a typeshed file or a custom type stub). The type checker requires type stubs to do its best job at analysis.

reportImportCycles.description: Diagnostics for cyclical import chains. These are not errors in Python, but they do slow down type analysis and often hint at architectural layering issues. Generally, they should be avoided.

reportUnusedImport.description: Diagnostics for an imported symbol that is not referenced within that file.

reportUnusedClass.description: Diagnostics for a class with a private name (starting with an underscore) that is not accessed.

reportUnusedFunction.description: Diagnostics for a function or method with a private name (starting with an underscore) that is not accessed.

reportUnusedVariable.description: Diagnostics for a variable that is not accessed.

reportDuplicateImport.description: Diagnostics for an imported symbol or module that is imported more than once.

reportWildcardImportFromLibrary.description: Diagnostics for an wildcard import from an external library.

reportAbstractUsage.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to instantiate an abstract or protocol class or use an abstract method.

reportArgumentType.description: Diagnostics for a type incompatibility for an argument to a call.

reportPossiblyUnboundVariable.description: Diagnostics for the use of variables that may be unbound on some code paths.

reportAssertTypeFailure.description: Diagnostics for a type incompatibility detected by a typing.assert_type call.

reportMissingSuperCall.description: Diagnostics for missing call to parent class for inherited `__init__` methods.

reportAssignmentType.description: Diagnostics for type incompatibilities for assignments.

reportUninitializedInstanceVariable.description: Diagnostics for instance variables that are not declared or initialized within class body or `__init__` method.

reportAttributeAccessIssue.description: Diagnostics for issues involving attribute accesses.

reportInvalidStringEscapeSequence.description: Diagnostics for invalid escape sequences used within string literals. The Python specification indicates that such sequences will generate a syntax error in future versions.

reportCallIssue.description: Diagnostics for issues involving call expressions and arguments.

reportUnknownParameterType.description: Diagnostics for input or return parameters for functions or methods that have an unknown type.

reportInconsistentOverload.description: Diagnostics for inconsistencies between function overload signatures and implementation.

reportUnknownArgumentType.description: Diagnostics for call arguments for functions or methods that have an unknown type.

reportIndexIssue.description: Diagnostics related to index operations and expressions.

reportUnknownLambdaType.description: Diagnostics for input or return parameters for lambdas that have an unknown type.

reportInvalidTypeArguments.description: Diagnostics for invalid type argument usage.

reportUnknownVariableType.description: Diagnostics for variables that have an unknown type..

reportNoOverloadImplementation.description: Diagnostics for an overloaded function or method with a missing implementation.

reportUnknownMemberType.description: Diagnostics for class or instance variables that have an unknown type.

reportOperatorIssue.description: Diagnostics for related to unary or binary operators.

reportMissingParameterType.description: Diagnostics for parameters that are missing a type annotation.

reportOptionalSubscript.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to subscript (index) a variable with an Optional type.

reportMissingTypeArgument.description: Diagnostics for generic class reference with missing type arguments.

reportOptionalMemberAccess.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to access a member of a variable with an Optional type.

reportInvalidTypeVarUse.description: Diagnostics for improper use of type variables in a function signature.

reportOptionalCall.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to call a variable with an Optional type.

reportCallInDefaultInitializer.description: Diagnostics for function calls within a default value initialization expression. Such calls can mask expensive operations that are performed at module initialization time.

reportOptionalIterable.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to use an Optional type as an iterable value (e.g. within a for statement).

reportUnnecessaryIsInstance.description: Diagnostics for 'isinstance' or 'issubclass' calls where the result is statically determined to be always (or never) true. Such calls are often indicative of a programming error.

reportOptionalContextManager.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to use an Optional type as a context manager (as a parameter to a with statement).

reportUnnecessaryCast.description: Diagnostics for 'cast' calls that are statically determined to be unnecessary. Such calls are sometimes indicative of a programming error.

reportOptionalOperand.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to use an Optional type as an operand to a binary or unary operator (like '+', '<<', '~').

reportUnnecessaryComparison.description: Diagnostics for '==' and '!=' comparisons that are statically determined to be unnecessary. Such calls are sometimes indicative of a programming error.

reportRedeclaration.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to declare the type of a symbol multiple times.

reportUnnecessaryContains.description: Diagnostics for 'in' operation that is statically determined to be unnecessary. Such operations are sometimes indicative of a programming error.

reportReturnType.description: Diagnostics related to function return type compatibility.

reportAssertAlwaysTrue.description: Diagnostics for 'assert' statement that will provably always assert. This can be indicative of a programming error.

reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess.description: Diagnostics for an attempt to access a non-required key within a TypedDict without a check for its presence.

reportUntypedFunctionDecorator.description: Diagnostics for function decorators that have no type annotations. These obscure the function type, defeating many type analysis features.

reportUntypedClassDecorator.description: Diagnostics for class decorators that have no type annotations. These obscure the class type, defeating many type analysis features.

reportUntypedBaseClass.description: Diagnostics for base classes whose type cannot be determined statically. These obscure the class type, defeating many type analysis features.

reportUntypedNamedTuple.description: Diagnostics when “namedtuple” is used rather than “NamedTuple”. The former contains no type information, whereas the latter does.

reportPrivateUsage.description: Diagnostics for incorrect usage of private or protected variables or functions. Protected class members begin with a single underscore _ and can be accessed only by subclasses. Private class members begin with a double underscore but do not end in a double underscore and can be accessed only within the declaring class. Variables and functions declared outside of a class are considered private if their names start with either a single or double underscore, and they cannot be accessed outside of the declaring module.

reportTypeCommentUsage.description: Diagnostics for usage of deprecated type comments.

reportPrivateImportUsage.description: Diagnostics for incorrect usage of symbol imported from a "py.typed" module that is not re-exported from that module.

reportSelfClsParameterName.description: Diagnostics for a missing or misnamed “self” parameter in instance methods and “cls” parameter in class methods. Instance methods in metaclasses (classes that derive from “type”) are allowed to use “cls” for instance methods.

reportConstantRedefinition.description: Diagnostics for attempts to redefine variables whose names are all-caps with underscores and numerals.

reportImplicitStringConcatenation.description: Diagnostics for two or more string literals that follow each other, indicating an implicit concatenation. This is considered a bad practice and often masks bugs such as missing commas.

reportDeprecated.description: Diagnostics for use of deprecated classes or functions.

reportInvalidStubStatement.description: Diagnostics for type stub statements that do not conform to PEP 484.

reportIncompatibleMethodOverride.description: Diagnostics for methods that override a method of the same name in a base class in an incompatible manner (wrong number of parameters, incompatible parameter types, or incompatible return type).

reportIncompleteStub.description: Diagnostics for the use of a module-level “__getattr__” function, indicating that the stub is incomplete.

reportIncompatibleVariableOverride.description: Diagnostics for overrides in subclasses that redefine a variable in an incompatible way.

reportInconsistentConstructor.description: Diagnostics for __init__ and __new__ methods whose signatures are inconsistent.

reportUnboundVariable.description: Diagnostics for the use of unbound variables.

reportOverlappingOverload.description: Diagnostics for function overloads that overlap in signature and obscure each other or have incompatible return types.

reportUnhashable.description: Diagnostics for the use of an unhashable object in a container that requires hashability.

reportUnsupportedDunderAll.description: Diagnostics for unsupported operations performed on __all__.

reportUnusedCallResult.description: Diagnostics for call expressions whose results are not consumed and are not None.

reportUnusedCoroutine.description: Diagnostics for call expressions that return a Coroutine and whose results are not consumed.

reportUnusedExpression.description: Diagnostics for simple expressions whose value is not used in any way.

reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment.description: Diagnostics for '# type: ignore' comments that have no effect.

basedpyright.disableLanguageServices.description: Disables type completion, definitions, and references.

basedpyright.importStrategy.description: Whether to use the version of pyright installed in the project (recommended) or the one bundled with the extension (not recommended).

basedpyright.disableTaggedHints.description: Disable hint diagnostics with special hints for grayed-out or strike-through text.

python.venvPath.description: Path to folder with a list of Virtual Environments.

python.pythonPath.description: Path to Python, you can use a custom version of Python.

basedpyright.disablePullDiagnostics.description: Disables the use of pull diagnostics from VS Code.

basedpyright.analysis.autoSearchPaths.description: Automatically add common search paths like 'src'?

basedpyright.analysis.include.description: Paths of directories or files that should be included. If no paths are specified, pyright defaults to the workspace root directory. Paths may contain wildcard characters ** (a directory or multiple levels of directories), * (a sequence of zero or more characters), or ? (a single character).

basedpyright.analysis.fileEnumerationTim.description: Timeout (in seconds) for file enumeration operations. Default is 10 seconds.
